summary: The agent implemented the Node-side size-limit behavior, but omitted the browser client implementation, causing all three client verification cases to time out. A separate multipart verifier case also assumes an undocumented private-helper signature.
quick_failure_summary: Browser requests never enforce the request or response size limits, so their callbacks are never invoked.

details.reasoning: The patch adds maxRequestSize() and hasSizeError() to the shared base and implements enforcement only in src/node/index.js. It leaves src/client.js unchanged, although the repository has a browser Request implementation that shares RequestBase and the prompt requires requests to abort on size-limit errors without limiting the scope to Node. The JUnit client_mock suite consequently times out for oversized upload, oversized download, and late-error handling. The trajectory also shows the agent inspected src/client.js but only added Node changes and ran Node-focused tests.
details.secondary_factors: The multipart delegation verifier wraps _sendMultipartBody(formData) and calls the original with only that argument, while the agent reasonably extracted it as _sendMultipartBody(formData, req). This undocumented private-method signature assumption produces the TypeError in that verifier case, but it is secondary to the missing browser behavior.

justification.issue_description: Missing maxRequestSize/maxResponseSize enforcement and single-callback handling in the browser XHR Request implementation.
justification.evidence: The prompt says that when either request or response size limit is exceeded, 'the request must abort and trigger a single callback' and does not restrict this to Node. The visible repository contains src/client.js, whose Request inherits the shared RequestBase prototype, constructs an XMLHttpRequest, sends payloads in Request.prototype._end, and handles upload/download progress. The solution patch modifies src/node/index.js and src/request-base.js but not src/client.js. junit_new.xml records three 10-second timeouts in test/node/client_mock.js.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented hidden edge case: the requested behavior is stated for Request generally, and browser support is a first-class visible implementation in the repository. A competent developer should apply the size-limit semantics to both Node and browser request paths or explicitly establish otherwise.

problem_assessment.notes: The central cross-runtime size-limit and callback requirements are clear and appropriately challenging. One multipart verifier assertion is overly coupled to an undocumented private helper signature: it assumes _sendMultipartBody obtains req from this rather than accepting req as an argument.

evidence: junit_base.xml reports 16 tests with 0 failures; junit_new.xml reports 13 tests with 5 failures.
The three client_mock failures are timeouts, while agent_solution.patch contains no src/client.js changes.

The multipart delegation failure is TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setHeader') after hidden_verify.js replaces _sendMultipartBody with a wrapper that calls original.call(this, formData), omitting the agent helper's second req argument.
The trajectory shows an unrelated full-suite IPv6 failure, but the agent performed no repeated workaround or debugging loop around it and it did not prevent focused Node validation.
environment_assessment.finding: The verifier should not require an undocumented _sendMultipartBody argument signature; its wrapper should forward all arguments. This is secondary to the agent's missing browser implementation.
